Quick Start: Your First SLA Program

This page walks through a complete chain with real commands: sla init generates the project skeleton → sla check runs the frontend check → sla build-exe compiles a native executable. After reading it, you will be able to create, check, and run an SLA project on your own.

Prerequisites

The SA toolchain is installed (see Installation and Building). Installing with the fully automatic installation package is recommended: after installation, both sa and sla are top-level commands, with no environment variables needed. When installing from source in dev mode, bringing SA_PLUGIN_DEV=1 along is recommended; the top-level sla command enters the plugin command dispatcher directly, and the spelling is the same under both installation methods.

The Three-Step Flow

# 任意目录直接可用（示例路径以 /tmp 为例）
sla init /tmp/sla_app                                    # 生成最小项目骨架
sla check /tmp/sla_app/src/main.sla                      # 词法/语法/类型检查
sla build-exe /tmp/sla_app/src/main.sla -o /tmp/main     # 编译为原生可执行文件
# 源码 dev 模式的写法（--dev 安装建议带环境变量）
SA_PLUGIN_DEV=1 sla init /tmp/sla_app
SA_PLUGIN_DEV=1 sla build-exe /tmp/sla_app/src/main.sla -o /tmp/main

When init succeeds, it outputs Initialized SLA binary project: <path> and the entry file path. After that, just run /tmp/main.

The Skeleton Generated by init

sla init [path] creates a minimal SLA binary project containing the following three files (it does not overwrite existing files with the same names):

FileContents
sa.modThe package manifest, of the form # generated by sla init plus one line package "sla_app" (the package name is taken from the directory name)
src/main.slaThe program entry point: fn main() -> i32 { return 0; };
.gitignoreIgnores .sla-cache/, .zig-cache/, .sa_cache/, zig-out/, *.out, *.sa.bc

Rewriting main.sla

Sla imports the SA top-level sa_std package directly. See the demo demos/rosetta/01_hello_world/main.sla:

@import "sa_std/io/print.sai"
@import "sa_std/fmt.sai"
@import "sa_std/string.sa"

fn main() -> i32 {
    println("hello, saasm");
    return 0;
};
NoteBy default, Sla's lifetime cleanup is managed by the compiler, so user-facing code needs no explicit release, and there is no drop keyword. Standard library paths are resolved from SA_STD_DIR by default (falling back to $HOME/projects/sci/sa_std when it is not set).

Intermediate Products and Other Common Commands

# 编译为经校验的 .sa 汇编文本
sla build src/main.sla --out /tmp/main.sa

# 直接编译为 SAB 字节码（默认写入托管缓存，--out 额外输出可见 .sab 文件）
sla sab build src/main.sla --out /tmp/main.sab

# 反汇编 SAB 用于调试
sla sab disasm /tmp/main.sab

# 各命令的完整参数说明见「命令行参考」章节

By default, build-exe takes the SA text path (the production path): it first emits a sibling .sa intermediate product, then delegates to the underlying sa build-exe. With an explicit --test-backend sab, it takes the SAB path instead: it writes the SAB bytes to the managed product path .sla-cache/sab/… and then delegates. A user-visible SAB file is written only when --out / --sab-out is passed explicitly.

Verifying the Installation with a Ready-Made Demo

# 运行目录：sa_plugin_sla 仓库根目录
sla check demos/rosetta/01_hello_world/main.sla
sla build demos/rosetta/01_hello_world/main.sla --out /tmp/01_hello_world.sa
sla build-exe demos/rosetta/01_hello_world/main.sla -o /tmp/01_hello_world
sla test demos/rosetta/01_hello_world/main.sla
WarningThe demos/rosetta tree is used to manually check semantic equivalence against the Rust reference implementation, and not all of it passes end to end; please verify items individually as needed, and do not assume the whole tree is ready.
